17.1.intro: A year of sales works best as a rhythm. Customers learn when to look, and you're never rushing. Deep discounts are only a last resort for slow stock.

steps.say: Pick a regular day and time for new products. Example: the first Thursday of each month, 7pm. Put the next 6 in your calendar.
steps.check: Your release dates are set and repeat monthly.
steps.lost: Pick one day each month for new products.

steps.say: Add gift days and special moments (Mother's Day, Valentine's Day). Pick a chosen set of products, not a store-wide discount.
steps.check: Each event has a product selection planned.
steps.lost: Add Mother's Day with 5 gift picks.

steps.say: Choose 3 to 4 big sales for the year. Black Friday is usually the biggest.
steps.check: Your big sales are in the calendar with dates.
steps.lost: Put Black Friday in your calendar.

steps.say: For slow stock, try gentle tools first: a free gift with purchase, bundles, VIP codes or gift cards.
steps.check: Slow stock has a plan that avoids deep discounts.
steps.lost: Bundle one slow product with a best seller.

17.2.intro: A launch has four parts. Each needs its own message.

steps.say: Before launch, tease the product. Open a waitlist and early-access sign-up.
steps.check: People sign up before the product is out.
steps.lost: Make a waitlist sign-up.

steps.say: On launch day, let VIPs (best customers) in first, then everyone.
steps.check: VIPs get a head start and feel looked after.
steps.lost: Email VIPs first on launch day.

steps.say: In the middle, release something new for 24 hours, like a new colour or a bundle.
steps.check: The launch gets a second spike.
steps.lost: Release one new colour for 24 hours.

steps.say: After launch, share reviews, results and restock news.
steps.check: Proof keeps sales going after launch week.
steps.lost: Share one review after launch.

17.3.intro: How you set up a launch depends on your spend. Your email list and warm audiences should hear first.

steps.say:
Choose where launch ads go (a rough rule of thumb).

- Spend about $1,000 a day or more: make a separate launch campaign.
- Spend less: add launch ads to your normal cold and warm campaigns.
steps.check: Launch ads have a home that fits your budget.
steps.lost: Under $1,000 a day? Add launch ads to your normal campaigns.

steps.say: Give warm audiences and your email list first access. Keep your always-on campaigns running.
steps.check: Your best people hear first, and new customers keep coming.
steps.lost: Don't switch off your normal campaigns.

17.4.intro: A big sale is a project with seven parts. Planning them in order makes the sale profitable.

steps.say: Set a target: last year's sales for this event times your growth rate. Example: $20,000 × 1.2 = $24,000. Check it against list size, budget and stock.
steps.check: You have a sales target you can actually support.
steps.lost: Take last year's sale number. Times your growth.

steps.say: Build the offer: a main offer, free gift levels (spend $100, get a gift), something new mid-sale, and a VIP perk. Check margin at every level.
steps.check: Every offer level still makes money.
steps.careful: A "was" price must be one you really charged for a while just before the sale. Fake "was" prices break the law. In the EU, it must be your lowest price in the last 30 days, counting earlier sale prices.
steps.lost: Pick one main offer. Check it still makes money.

steps.say: Pick a theme: a name, a look and a message that stand out.
steps.check: The sale has a name and a look.
steps.lost: Give your sale a name.

steps.say: Plan the ad budget for each day of each phase (hype, launch, middle, finish), and the split between normal and sale campaigns.
steps.check: Every sale day has a planned budget.
steps.lost: Write a budget for launch day.

steps.say: List the ads you need for each phase and audience (cold, warm, hot). Plan emails and texts too (Lesson 16.13).
steps.check: Ads and messages are planned for every phase.
steps.lost: List the ads for launch day.

steps.say: Get the site ready: sale pages and banners, no site changes in the last 2 weeks (a code freeze), and every discount code tested.
steps.check: The site is ready and steady before launch.
steps.lost: Test every discount code.

steps.say: Check stock, packing helpers, gift stock and shipping cut-off dates.
steps.check: You can send out all the orders you plan to get.
steps.lost: Check you have enough stock.

17.5.intro: The build-up gets people excited before the sale. Then launch day starts with a crowd.

steps.say: Run sign-up ads and teasers for 3 to 5 days before the sale.
steps.check: Your early-access list grows each day.
steps.lost: Run one sign-up ad for 3 days.

steps.say: Track the cost per sign-up, and how many page visitors sign up.
steps.check: You know what the hype costs.
steps.lost: Divide ad spend by sign-ups.

steps.say: Move budget from normal campaigns to the hype campaign slowly. Never cut normal campaigns to zero.
steps.check: Normal campaigns keep learning and bringing new customers.
steps.lost: Move a little budget, not all of it.

17.6.intro: Running the sale is a daily routine. Judge the whole event, not one day.

steps.say: Set up sale campaigns: a copy of your best cold campaign, a cold campaign with combined audiences and exclusions, a mixed campaign with no exclusions, warm campaigns, and hot campaigns (add to cart and checkout).
steps.check: All sale campaigns are built and paused before launch.
steps.lost: Copy your best cold campaign. Pause it until launch.

steps.say: Set spending limits on every sale campaign.
steps.check: Nothing can overspend.
steps.lost: Add a spending limit to each one.

steps.say: Each day, check MER (all ad spend as a share of all sales) against your plan. Check stock, site speed and tired ads too.
steps.check: You catch problems the same day.
steps.lost: Check MER once a day.

steps.say: In the middle, add a new offer, fresh ads, and an email with a new reason to buy.
steps.check: The middle of the sale gets a boost.
steps.lost: Send one email with something new.

steps.say: Finish strong with last-chance ads, final emails and texts.
steps.check: The last day has its own push.
steps.careful: Quiet days in the middle are normal. Don't panic and cut spend.
steps.lost: Send one last-chance email.

17.7.intro: After a sale there's always a slow patch. How you handle it decides how many new buyers you keep.

steps.say: Turn normal campaigns back up in steps over a week. Not all at once.
steps.check: Campaigns recover without a spending shock.
steps.lost: Raise budgets a little each day.

steps.say: Check new buyers are getting your after-purchase emails.
steps.check: New customers get thanks and how-to tips.
steps.lost: Check your post-purchase flow is on.

steps.say: Compare sales with your target, MER, new customers and stock left. Write down one thing to do better.
steps.check: You have a short review with one improvement.
steps.lost: Write one thing to do better next time.

steps.say: Wait 7 days before final numbers. Ad apps keep adding late sales for about a week.
steps.check: Your review uses numbers from 7 days after the sale.
steps.lost: Wait a week, then review.

steps.say: For the next 2 to 4 weeks, run no new discount. Show full-price news or best-seller stories, and nudge new buyers to a second order (Lesson 16.17).
steps.check: A plan for the next few weeks with no discount.
steps.lost: Post one full-price product story.

17.8.intro: If a sale is behind plan, it's usually one of five things. Find it fast, then fix it without breaking trust.

steps.say: Check the five causes: an offer weaker than competitors', an offer that's not clear in the first seconds of ads, a site problem, a list that's too small, or bad timing.
steps.check: You've named the likely cause.
steps.lost: Is your offer clear in the first second of your ad?

steps.say: Pick one rescue: add a free gift level, release something new, send a stronger email, or move budget to warm audiences.
steps.check: A rescue is live within hours.
steps.careful: Only extend the sale if it won't break trust. Customers notice fake "last chances", and stores have paid fines for countdown timers that reset.
steps.lost: Add a free gift level.

17.9.intro: Start simple and add one layer to each sale.

steps.say: Find your level in the table: Starter, Seasoned or Advanced.
steps.check: You know your level.
steps.lost: New to sales? You are Starter.

steps.say: Add one thing from the next level to your next sale. Keep the rest the same.
steps.check: Each sale is a bit more advanced.
steps.lost: Pick just one new thing.

steps.say: After the sale, note what you added and whether it paid off.
steps.check: You know whether to keep it.
steps.lost: Do it in your sale review.

17.10.intro: Plan the whole busy season, not one weekend. In 2026, Black Friday is 27 November and Cyber Monday is 30 November. Helix adds the plan to your calendar from 1 August.

steps.say: All year, test ad ideas and offers, and grow your list. Then you know what works before the busy season.
steps.check: You have proven ads and a bigger list by August.
steps.lost: Test one ad idea this month.

steps.say:
Put the Black Friday stages in your Helix calendar.

- August: review last year. Set targets. Test new ads.
- September: order stock 10 to 12 weeks out. Lock the offer.
- October: finish ads. Warm up audiences. Build email flows.
- November: launch. Check numbers daily.
- December and January: review and plan next year.
steps.check: Every stage is in your calendar with dates.
steps.lost: Find this month on the list. Do that part.

steps.say: Add gift campaigns with delivery cut-off dates ("order by the 18th for Christmas").
steps.check: Shoppers know the last safe day to order.
steps.lost: Add your Christmas order-by date to your site.

steps.say: Plan for Boxing Day and the quiet weeks after (sometimes called the fifth quarter). Ad costs often drop then, so new customers can be cheaper.
steps.check: You have a plan for late December and January.
steps.lost: Plan one January campaign.

steps.say: Add end of financial year sales where they matter (30 June in Australia), and Valentine's, Mother's and Father's Day gift picks.
steps.check: Your year has every key date planned.
steps.lost: Add Mother's Day to your calendar.

17.11.intro: Big sales use every channel at once. One missed setting can cost a day of sales. Tick this list a week before.

steps.say: Check Meta and Google sale campaigns are built and switched off.
steps.check: Campaigns are ready to switch on.
steps.lost: Check your sale campaigns are built and off.

steps.say: Check sale prices and promo pictures are in your product feed.
steps.check: Shopping ads will show sale prices.
steps.lost: Check one sale price in the feed.

steps.say: Check emails and texts are scheduled, and flows switch to sale versions at the right time.
steps.check: Messages go out by themselves.
steps.lost: Check your launch email is scheduled.

steps.say: Check free posts and creator posts are scheduled.
steps.check: Social is ready.
steps.lost: Schedule your launch post.

steps.say: Test site banners, sale pages and discount rules with a real test order.
steps.check: Discounts work properly at checkout.
steps.lost: Place one test order with the discount.

steps.say: Give customer service saved replies for common sale questions.
steps.check: The team can answer fast during the rush.
steps.lost: Write 3 saved replies.

17.12.intro: One big sale a year makes cash bumpy and leaves stock sitting. One or two smaller, planned sales clear old stock and bring old customers back.

steps.say: Pick a window at least 8 weeks away from your biggest sale. Choose a reason: clearing a season's stock, end of financial year, or your brand's birthday.
steps.check: You have 3 to 5 days and a reason customers will believe.
steps.lost: Pick 3 days and one reason.

steps.say: Choose what's on sale: slow stock and last season's colours first. Best sellers only at a smaller discount, or not at all. Check each one's margin in your profit setup.
steps.check: A product list where every line still makes money after marketing.
steps.lost: Put your slowest product on sale first.

steps.say: Plan it in Helix Calendar: a teaser email 3 days before, a launch email and text, a middle-day reminder, a last-chance email, plus ads to past buyers and site visitors.
steps.check: The sale and its messages are in your calendar with dates.
steps.lost: Put the launch email in your calendar.

steps.say:
When it ends, write down how it went.

1. Record sales, profit, units cleared, and new versus returning customers.
2. Write one thing to change next time.
steps.check: You know if the sale made money and if you'd repeat it.
steps.careful: Count big and small sales together. The more often you run sales, the more customers wait for the next one. Keep them planned, rare and with a clear reason.
steps.lost: Write down the profit. Was it worth it?

17.13.intro: A discount takes money from every order. Work out how many more orders you need, then pick an offer you can reach.

steps.say: Open **Numbers** in Helix. Find your price and your profit on one order before ads.
steps.check: Two numbers, like $60 price and $30 profit.
steps.lost: Find your profit on one order.

steps.say: Work out the real discount: the discount times the share of orders that use it. 20% off used by 70 of every 100 orders = 14%.
steps.check: You know the real discount.
steps.lost: Multiply the discount by how many people use it.

steps.say: Divide normal profit by discounted profit. At 20% off a $60 item, $30 becomes $18. $30 ÷ $18 = 1.67.
steps.check: You know you need about 1.67 times the orders.
steps.lost: Normal profit ÷ sale profit.

steps.say: Check your target against your list, your ad budget and your stock. Pick the smallest discount that hits it.
steps.check: One offer you can actually reach.
steps.lost: Pick the smallest discount that works.

steps.say: Split the target: for example 35% launch days, 30% middle, 35% final days. Divide by the days in each part.
steps.check: A target for every sale day.
steps.lost: Write a sales number for each day.

steps.say: Divide sale profit by sale price: $18 ÷ $48 = 37.5%. Keep ad spend under that share of sales. Check it daily.
steps.check: One MER limit you check each day.
steps.careful: Many other tools show MER the other way round. Helix 25% = 4x there.
steps.lost: Keep ad spend under 37% of sales.
